Using the latest version of Claude Code, macOS and Linux users can now send messages between different work sessions to share findings, ask questions, and coordinate work. Details are as follows.

Claude Code adds cross-work-session messaging feature

Anthropic recently announced a new feature that should be very practical for users who frequently run multiple Claude Code work sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code version v2.1.224, different work sessions can send messages to each other, sharing updates and other relevant information. This feature is especially useful for multiple work sessions handling different parts of the same project simultaneously.

The following is the documentation released by Anthropic regarding this new feature:

Anthropic stated that the best use cases for this new feature include: handing over work, coordinating parallel work trees, checking the status of long-running programs, and replying to messages across machines.

The company added that users do not need to write the message content themselves. Users only need to include in their prompts what they wish to convey, and Claude will write the actual message on their behalf.

It is worth noting that the cross-work-session messaging feature does not apply to approving permission requests or changing settings. Commands such as /compact will be sent as plain text rather than being executed as actual commands; and if handling messages requires permissions, the recipient will still request approval from the user.
